findings.message:
[P1] Duplicate HUB_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME import breaks passport cutover tests

The added import on line 27 imports `HUB_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` from `../src/session_cookie.ts` even though line 25 already declares the same binding. A module cannot lexically declare the same name twice, so loading this file is a syntax error and `bun test tests/passport_cutover_test.ts`, which `bun run check` executes, fails before any test runs. Delete the duplicate import.

tests/passport_cutover_test.ts:27-27

[P2] Duplicate rejection also blocks login when a sibling plants the CSRF cookie

`cookieValue` now returns an empty string whenever a name appears more than once, and `loginCsrfToken` (line 42) reuses that helper, so the rejection also applies to `dua_login_csrf`. A sibling can plant `dua_login_csrf` with `Domain=prospector.sh`; once `/login` adds the host-only copy the browser sends both, the server then treats the expected nonce as empty while `public/auth.js` still sends the first document cookie, so `loginSubmissionError` returns `invalid_login_csrf` (403) on every attempt. Previously the first-value parser let login proceed, so this turns a sibling-planted cookie into a persistent login lockout rather than the shadowing defense the change intends. Scope the duplicate rejection to the `__Host-` session cookie (or read a `__Host-` prefixed CSRF cookie) instead.

src/session_cookie.ts:26-29

summary: The __Host- session cookie, plaintext issuance guard, duplicate rejection and Chromium sibling-domain regression are present, but the cutover test file redeclares the session cookie import and the shared duplicate rejection makes a sibling-planted CSRF cookie a persistent login lockout.

evidence: src/session_cookie.ts names the session cookie __Host-dua_session and always emits Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure with no Domain attribute.
hubSessionCookie and clearHubSessionCookie return an empty string unless the request is https or a loopback host, so no production session cookie is issued over plaintext HTTP.
cookieValue returns an empty value when the session cookie name appears more than once, so ambiguous duplicate session-cookie requests are rejected.
tests/session_cookie_browser_test.ts adds a Chromium sibling-domain regression proving a parent-domain duplicate cannot shadow or lock out the hub session.
